open_points.subject: sandbox scratch-total measurement failure
open_points.text: The scratch total is measured once, when the environment has ended
open_points.question: What outcome and process behavior apply if the parent cannot enumerate or stat the exchange directory completely when measuring the scratch total?
options: Record the execution as `crashed` and continue
Record `crashed` with `cleanup_failed` and stop the kernel
Answer an internal error without an execution outcome
open_points.default_guess: Record `crashed` with `cleanup_failed` and stop the kernel, because the resource result cannot be confirmed.

open_points.subject: exclusion of parent-created files from scratch total
open_points.text: the files the parent put there excluded
open_points.question: Is exclusion determined by the original inode, by the original path, or only while the original file remains unchanged, when agent code modifies, renames, deletes, replaces or hard-links a parent-created file?
options: Exclude the originally staged inode wherever it is linked
Exclude the originally staged paths regardless of replacement
Exclude only unchanged original files; count replacements or modifications
open_points.default_guess: Exclude the originally staged inodes, and count any replacement inode.

open_points.subject: meaning of links in scratch accounting
open_points.text: the apparent sizes of the distinct regular files (each inode once) under the exchange directory, the files the parent put there excluded; directories and links count nothing
open_points.question: Does “links count nothing” mean only symbolic links, or does it also exclude regular files reached through hard links despite the instruction to count each regular-file inode once?
options: Only symbolic links count nothing; a hard-linked regular-file inode counts once
All links, including hard-linked entries, count nothing
A hard-linked inode counts only when one of its entries is not treated as a link
open_points.default_guess: Treat “links” as symbolic links; count each regular-file inode once regardless of its hard-link count.
